about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Lazi Ji Chongqing Chilli Chicken
recipes.summary: Crisp fried chicken pieces buried in dried chillies and Sichuan pepper, the Chongqing bar-snack classic.

items: 600g boneless chicken thigh, cut into 2cm pieces

steps: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine and cornflour until each piece is coated.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok and shallow-fry the chicken in 2 batches for 4 minutes each, until golden and crisp. Lift out.
Wipe the wok, add a little oil if needed, Stir-fry the chillies and peppercorns for 30 seconds until fragrant but not burnt.
Add the garlic and ginger for 15 seconds, return the chicken and toss for 1 minute until well coated. Scatter with sesame and serve with the rice.
notes: Food safety: fry the chicken until the thickest piece reaches at least 75°C. Wash hands and board after raw chicken. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 15 minutes marinating. Chillies are for flavour, not for eating.

recipes.title: Gan Bian Si Ji Dou Dry-Fried Green Beans
recipes.summary: Blistered green beans with crisp pork mince, preserved vegetable and chilli, a Sichuan favourite with rice.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the beans for 5 minutes, turning, until the skins wrinkle and blister. Lift out.
Add the pork mince and stir-fry for 3 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through.
Add the chilli bean paste, chillies and garlic for 30 seconds, then return the beans with the soy sauce and sugar and toss for 1 minute.
Finish with the sesame oil and serve with the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince until no pink remains and it reaches at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Cong You Ji Cantonese Spring Onion Ginger Chicken
recipes.summary: Poached chicken pieces under a hot oil sauce of spring onion and ginger, Cantonese banquet style.
steps: Put the chicken in a pot with the sliced ginger and the first tbsp of salt, cover with water and bring to a gentle simmer for 20 minutes until cooked through.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Mix the spring onions, grated ginger, 1 tsp salt and soy sauce in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the oil until just smoking and pour it over the spring onion mixture; it will sizzle for about 10 seconds.
Lift out the chicken, drain well, chop through the bones and spoon the sauce over. Serve with the rice and cucumber.
notes: Food safety: the chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part and the juices run clear. Pour hot oil carefully. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Zheng Yu Cantonese Steamed Fish with Ginger and Soy
recipes.summary: Whole-fillet steamed fish with a scalding oil finish, light, clean and ready in minutes.

items: 3 tbsp ginger, cut into fine matchsticks
4 spring onions, cut into fine strips

steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Lay the fish on a heatproof plate, sprinkle with the Shaoxing wine and half the ginger, and steam over boiling water for 8 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Steam the bok choy beside it for the last 2 minutes until just tender.
Pour away the liquid from the plate, scatter over the spring onions and remaining ginger, and drizzle with the soy sauce.
Heat the neutral and sesame oils until shimmering and pour over the top. Serve with the rice.
notes: Food safety: steam the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Fen Zheng Rou Rice-Flour Steamed Pork
recipes.summary: Pork belly coated in toasted spiced rice flour and steamed until meltingly soft, a Sichuan and Hunan home dish.
steps: Toast the rice, peppercorns and star anise in a dry pan for 5 minutes until golden, cool, then grind coarsely.
Mix the pork with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, chilli bean paste, ginger and sugar. Fold in the ground rice until every slice is coated.
Lay the sweet potato in a heatproof dish and arrange the pork on top.
Steam over simmering water for 80 minutes, topping up the water as needed, until the pork is very tender.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve straight from the dish.
notes: Food safety: the pork must reach at least 70°C throughout; steaming this long takes it well past that. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 30 minutes marinating.

recipes.title: San Bei Ji Taiwanese Three-Cup Chicken
recipes.summary: Chicken braised in a cup each of sesame oil, soy and rice wine with ginger, garlic and plenty of basil.

items: 800g chicken thigh, bone in, chopped into pieces

steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the sesame oil in a wok over medium heat and fry the ginger, garlic and chillies for 2 minutes until golden at the edges.
Add the chicken and sear for 5 minutes, turning, until browned all over.
Add the soy sauce, rice wine and sugar, cover and cook for 12 minutes until the sauce is thick and clinging.
Toss through the basil until just wilted and serve with the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to at least 75°C at the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Yan Su Ji Taiwanese Salt and Pepper Chicken
recipes.summary: Night-market fried chicken pieces dusted with white pepper, five-spice and salt, finished with fried basil.

items: 600g boneless chicken thigh, cut into bite-size pieces

steps: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce and rice wine until coated.
Coat each piece well in the sweet potato flour, pressing it on, and let sit for 5 minutes so it clings.
Heat the oil in a wok and shallow-fry the chicken in batches for 4 minutes each until deep golden and crisp. Lift out.
Fry the basil and garlic in the same oil for 20 seconds until crisp, then lift out.
Toss the chicken with the pepper, five-spice and salt, and top with the basil and garlic.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches at least 75°C inside. Keep hot oil away from water. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 20 minutes marinating.

recipes.title: Tang Cu Pai Gu Sweet and Sour Spare Ribs
recipes.summary: Sticky pork ribs in a glossy black vinegar and sugar glaze, a Shanghai and Zhejiang home favourite.

items: 800g pork spare ribs, cut into 4cm pieces

steps: Put the ribs in a pot with the ginger, cover with cold water and bring to the boil, then simmer for 5 minutes until the scum rises. Drain and rinse.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok over low heat, add the sugar and stir for 3 minutes until amber, then add the ribs and toss to coat.
Add the vinegar, soy sauces, wine and water, cover and simmer for 35 minutes until the ribs are tender.
Uncover and boil hard for 5 minutes until the sauce is thick and sticky. Serve with the rice.
notes: Food safety: the pork must reach at least 70°C; simmering until tender takes it well past that. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Zi Ran Yang Rou Xinjiang Cumin Lamb
recipes.summary: Fast, fierce wok-fried lamb with toasted cumin, chilli and onion, the signature flavour of Xinjiang.

items: 2 tbsp cumin seeds, toasted and crushed

steps: Toss the lamb with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine and cornflour. Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over very high heat and sear the lamb in 2 batches for 2 minutes each, until browned. Lift out.
Add the remaining oil, the onion and garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes until charred at the edges.
Return the lamb with the cumin and chilli flakes and toss for 1 minute.
Scatter with the coriander and serve with the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the lamb until it reaches at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 15 minutes marinating.

recipes.title: Bi Feng Tang Typhoon Shelter Prawns
recipes.summary: Hong Kong prawns showered in crisp garlic, chilli and fermented black beans, finished with a hot wok toss.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Pat the prawns dry and dust with the cornflour. Fry in the hot oil for 2 minutes until pink and crisp, then lift out.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp of oil. Fry the garlic for 2 minutes until golden and crisp, then lift out onto paper.
Add the black beans and chillies for 30 seconds, return the prawns, pour in the wine and toss for 1 minute.
Add the garlic, spring onions and salt, toss, and serve with the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C. Contains shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Hong Kong Baked Pork Chop Rice
recipes.summary: Cha chaan teng style: fried pork chops on egg fried rice, smothered in tomato sauce and baked until bubbling.

items: 4 boneless pork loin chops, about 150g each

steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes, then spread out to cool. Toss the chops with the soy sauce, pepper and cornflour and pan-fry in 1 tbsp oil for 3 minutes each side until golden. Slice.
Fry the onion in 1 tbsp oil for 4 minutes, add the passata, ketchup and sugar and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Scramble the eggs in the remaining oil, add the rice and stir-fry for 3 minutes until hot and loose. Spread in a baking dish.
Lay the pork on the rice, spoon over the sauce and top with the mozzarella.
Bake at 220C for 12 minutes until the cheese is golden and the sauce bubbles.
notes: Food safety: the pork must reach at least 70°C; check after baking. Cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Ebi Furai Panko Fried Prawns
recipes.summary: Straight, crisp panko prawns served with shredded cabbage, lemon and tonkatsu sauce.

items: 16 large raw prawns, peeled and tails left on

steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Make 3 small cuts along the belly of each prawn and press flat so they stay straight. Season with the salt.
Coat in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and shallow-fry the prawns in 2 batches for 2 minutes each side until golden. Drain.
Serve on the cabbage with lemon, tonkatsu sauce and the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C. Contains shellfish, egg and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Nasu Dengaku Miso-Glazed Aubergine
recipes.summary: Seared aubergine halves with a sweet miso glaze grilled until bubbling, with sesame and rice.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Score the aubergine flesh in a crosshatch, brush with the oil and roast cut-side down at 220C for 15 minutes until soft.
Warm the miso, mirin, sugar and sake in a small pan over low heat for 3 minutes until smooth and glossy.
Turn the aubergines, spread with the miso glaze and grill for 4 minutes until bubbling and lightly charred.
Scatter with the sesame seeds and spring onions and serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Shioyaki Salt-Grilled Barramundi
recipes.summary: Salted barramundi fillets grilled until the skin crackles, served with grated daikon and lemon.
steps: Salt the fish on both sides. Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes, while the salt draws out moisture; pat the fish dry.
Heat the grill to high. Brush the fish with the oil and grill skin-side up for 6 minutes until the skin blisters and the flesh is opaque.
Mix the grated daikon with the soy sauce.
Serve the fish with the daikon, lemon, green beans and rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Buta no Shogayaki Japanese Ginger Pork
recipes.summary: Thin pork slices pan-fried in a sweet-salty ginger sauce, the everyday teishoku favourite.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar and ginger. Toss the pork in half of it for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pan over high heat and fry the onion for 2 minutes, then add the pork in a single layer and cook for 3 minutes until browned.
Pour in the rest of the sauce and cook for 1 minute until glossy.
Serve on the cabbage with the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork until no pink remains and it reaches at least 70°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Teriyaki Buri Glazed Yellowtail
recipes.summary: Pan-seared yellowtail steaks glazed in a homemade teriyaki until sticky and lacquered.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar.
Sear the fish in the oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes each side until golden.
Pour in the sauce and cook for 3 minutes, spooning it over, until thick and glossy and the fish is opaque.
Steam the broccolini for 3 minutes until tender. Serve with the fish, rice and sesame seeds.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Domi Gui Korean Grilled Snapper
recipes.summary: Salted snapper fillets pan-grilled until crisp, served with rice and a soy-sesame dipping sauce.
steps: Salt the fillets and rest for 10 minutes; pat dry.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the fillets in the oil over medium-high heat, skin-side down first, for 4 minutes each side until crisp and opaque.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, gochugaru and spring onions for the dip.
Serve the fish with the dip, rice and cucumber.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 10 minutes salting.

recipes.title: Tteokgalbi Grilled Short Rib Patties
recipes.summary: Sweet soy beef and pork rib-style patties, pan-grilled, the royal court Korean classic.
steps: Mix both minces with the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, pear and pine nuts, kneading for 2 minutes until sticky. Rest for 15 minutes.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Shape into 8 oval patties about 2cm thick.
Pan-fry in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes each side until browned and cooked through.
Serve with the rice and lettuce leaves.
notes: Food safety: mince must be cooked right through; patties reach at least 75°C inside. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 15 minutes resting.

recipes.title: Jangjorim Soy-Braised Beef with Eggs
recipes.summary: Beef simmered in soy, garlic and green chilli until tender and shredded, a staple of the Korean table.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Put the beef, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger and water in a pot, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the eggs and chillies and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce is reduced and glossy.
Shred the beef a little with two forks, stir in the sesame oil and serve with the rice.
notes: Food safety: beef must reach at least 71°C; simmered until tender it will. Boil the eggs until the yolk is firm. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Saengseon Jeon Korean Pan-Fried Fish Fillets
recipes.summary: White fish fillets coated in flour and egg, shallow-fried to a golden coat and served with soy dipping sauce.

items: 600g firm white fish fillets, cut into 5cm pieces

steps: Season the fish with the salt. Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Dredge each piece in flour, then dip in egg.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes each side, until golden and the fish flakes.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and gochugaru for the dip.
Serve the fish hot with the dip and rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C; eggs are fully cooked in the coating. Contains fish and egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Gai Tod Hat Yai Southern Thai Fried Chicken
recipes.summary: Hat Yai fried chicken marinated in coriander root and white pepper, topped with crisp fried shallots.

items: 800g chicken thigh, bone in, cut into pieces

steps: Mix the chicken with the coriander roots, garlic, pepper, fish sauce and rice flour. Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the oil to 170C and fry the chicken in 2 batches for 10 minutes each until deep golden.
Check that the thickest piece is cooked right through, then drain on paper.
Scatter with the fried shallots.
Serve with the sweet chilli sauce and rice.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Keep hot oil away from water. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 30 minutes marinating.

recipes.title: Moo Tod Gratiem Thai Garlic Pepper Pork
recipes.summary: Pork slices fried with plenty of garlic and black pepper, served with rice and a fried egg.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Crush the garlic, coriander root and pepper together and mix with the oyster sauce and fish sauce.
Toss the pork in the paste and fry in 2 tbsp oil over high heat for 5 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set and the yolks are firm.
Serve the pork with the rice, eggs and cucumber.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches at least 70°C. Fry the eggs until yolks are firm. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 15 minutes marinating.

recipes.title: Nam Tok Neua Thai Waterfall Beef
recipes.summary: Grilled steak sliced and dressed with lime, fish sauce, chilli, toasted rice and mint, an Isaan classic.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Toast the 2 tbsp of rice in a dry pan for 4 minutes until deep golden, then grind coarsely.
Grill the steak over high heat for 4 minutes each side, rest for 5 minutes, then slice thinly.
Toss the beef with the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, chilli, shallots and ground rice.
Fold through the herbs and serve with the lettuce and rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the steak to at least 63°C and rest for 3 minutes; slices cooked through reach 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Pla Kapong Neung Thai Lime Steamed Barramundi
recipes.summary: Whole-fillet fish steamed and drenched in a punchy garlic, chilli, lime and coriander dressing.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Put the fish and lemongrass on a heatproof plate and steam over boiling water for 10 minutes, until opaque and flaking.
Steam the bok choy for the last 2 minutes until just tender.
Whisk the garlic, chillies, lime juice, fish sauce and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Pour over the hot fish, scatter with the coriander and serve with the rice.
notes: Food safety: steam the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Pla Pao Thai Salt-Crusted Grilled Fish
recipes.summary: Whole fish packed in salt and lemongrass, baked until the flesh is moist, served with a spicy seafood dip.

items: 1 whole snapper, about 1.2kg, gutted and scaled

steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Stuff the fish with half the lemongrass and the galangal, and bed it on the rest of the lemongrass in a baking tray.
Pack the salt over the fish and bake at 220C for 25 minutes until the flesh is opaque.
Mix the lime juice, fish sauce, chillies, garlic and sugar for the dip.
Crack away the salt, lift the flesh from the bones and serve with the dip and rice.
notes: Food safety: the fish must be opaque and flake easily, at least 63°C at the thickest part. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
